metaTitle: How to Keep Lab-Grown Diamonds Sparkling
metaDescription: Keep lab-grown diamond jewellery sparkling by preventing oil and product build-up, handling it correctly, cleaning safely and checking the setting.
title: How to Keep Lab-Grown Diamond Jewellery Sparkling
subtitle: Journal

content.text: Lab-grown diamonds do not gradually run out of sparkle. Their cut and polished facets continue to interact with light, but skin oils, lotion, soap film and dust can cover those surfaces and mute the visible result.

The best care strategy is prevention: touch the diamond less, apply products before jewellery, remove it for residue-heavy activities, wipe compatible pieces after wear and clean only by the method approved for the complete item.

Keep lab-grown diamond jewellery sparkling by handling it by the metal rather than touching the stone, putting it on after skincare and perfume have dried, removing it before showering, swimming, cooking, exercise and household cleaning, and wiping compatible surfaces with a clean lint-free cloth after wear. Pay attention to residue behind the diamond, where light interaction can be affected. Use the approved gentle cleaning routine when film appears, inspect settings before and after, store pieces separately and arrange professional care when dullness persists.

items.question: Do lab-grown diamonds lose their sparkle over time?
items.answer: They do not run out of sparkle, but oil, lotion, soap film and dust can temporarily mute their light performance.

items.question: Why does my lab-grown diamond look dull?
items.answer: Surface or underside residue and different lighting are common causes. Persistent dullness after an approved clean needs professional assessment.

items.question: Does cleaning improve a diamond’s cut?
items.answer: No. Cleaning removes surface interference; it cannot change proportions, symmetry, polish or cut grade.

items.question: Why should I avoid touching the diamond?
items.answer: Finger oils transfer easily to diamond surfaces and can reduce visible brilliance and fire.

items.question: Should jewellery go on before or after perfume?
items.answer: Apply perfume and other products first, let them dry, then put jewellery on last.

items.question: Can I wear diamond jewellery in the shower?
items.answer: Removing it helps prevent soap and product film and avoids unnecessary risk to the setting and other materials.

items.question: Why is the back of a diamond important?
items.answer: Oil and dirt beneath the stone can interfere with light interaction and make the face-up appearance look duller.

items.question: Can a microfibre cloth keep diamonds sparkling?
items.answer: An approved clean cloth can remove light surface residue between cleans, but it may not reach behind the stone.

items.question: Can I use toothpaste to restore sparkle?
items.answer: No. Toothpaste is abrasive and can scratch metal or finishes and lodge in settings.

items.question: Does an ultrasonic cleaner create more sparkle?
items.answer: It removes some residue but does not improve cut; use it only after professional approval of the complete piece.

items.question: Does lighting change how a clean diamond looks?
items.answer: Yes. Diamonds reflect their surroundings, so brightness, fire and contrast vary across lighting environments.

items.question: What if safe cleaning does not restore the sparkle?
items.answer: Stop repeating the process and have the diamond, setting and finish assessed by a qualified jeweller.
